attackListDisposition.detail: Decision 3 states 'DR-111 stays OPEN. No SATISFIED.' Decision 4 states 'Does not edit file 08 (MF-6). No freeze motion. No blueprint. Does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/.' The Alternatives section rejects 'Mark SATISFIED' and rejects 'Treat dual ACCEPT as application. Rejected: binds NOTHING.' Readiness effect is stated as Zero. I found no QUALIFIED or DEMONSTRATED claim anywhere in the draft. The subject artifact independently corroborates the boundary: v5 carries status CANDIDATE-NOT-APPLIED, sealRecommendation DO-NOT-SEAL, binds NOTHING, documentClass DESIGN-CONTRACT-CANDIDATE, and its own whatThisDoesNotDo opens with 'Does not SATISFY DR-111 until independently reviewed and recorded by a later D-000 MF-6' and closes with 'Does not authorize docs/v2/implementation/.'

attackListDisposition.attack: Treating advisories as blockers or pretending they do not exist
attackListDisposition.result: REFUTED - the advisory accounting is exact
attackListDisposition.detail: Decision 2 names them individually - 'Claude ADV-1/ADV-2; Codex CMCV5-A1' - and I confirmed those are the actual ids in the two verdict files: the Claude verdict carries advisories ADV-1 ('The v2 roster rename left a dangling internal reference in reviewGuidance') and ADV-2 ('/honestyRepairsFromV3 is superseded but is neither suffixed Historical nor listed in the Historical enumeration'); the Codex verdict carries CMCV5-A1 ('/basedOn/method calls the newly added historical key not a v5 path after listing it as a v5 succession delta'). The draft neither inflates them into blockers nor suppresses them: 'not blockers. They do not prevent this recording. They remain owed as honesty work on a successor, not as a reason to withhold the recording.' That is the same treatment D-035 gave A1-A6 and D-042 gave P2-01/02/03 and PT2-CX-A1. The Alternatives section additionally rejects waiting for a v6 that folds them, with the gate stated - '0 blockers and 0 SHOULD-FIX is the gate; advisories travel.'

attackListDisposition.attack: Claiming a lock is now producible
attackListDisposition.result: REFUTED - the draft denies it and the subject artifact agrees
attackListDisposition.detail: Decision 3: 'This recording does not make any lock producible.' The subject's /lockJoin states the opposite of producibility in its own words: 'no lock of any form - exact-pin or constrained, one component or many - is producible until this row closes with evaluable windows', and 'This artifact does not itself emit a lock or a lock evaluator; it supplies the window/compatibility meaning a later DR-103 successor would consume.' I also note the subject's ATTRIBUTION paragraph is careful in a way that matters here: it records that D-013's accepted schemas.v2 states only the narrower constrained-request rule, that the widening to exact-pin and cardinality is PROPOSED here and written in unaccepted successors, and that 'citing a successor does not accept it, does not claim it is the live head, and does not lend D-013's acceptance to the wider rule.' D-103 records that artifact without importing the wider rule as accepted, which is the correct reading.

attackListDisposition.attack: Opening D-056 Class A / SATISFIED while windows and S-EVIDENCE remain
attackListDisposition.result: REFUTED - the draft applies the correct gate and the gate genuinely fails
attackListDisposition.detail: Decision 3: 'D-056 Class A is not opened by this recording: leftover is not only execution/measurement.' I read D-056's operative text: its five Eligibility gates include 'remainder is only execution / measurement', so the draft is citing the right test. The test genuinely fails for DR-111 on measured grounds, not by assertion: the subject's /numericWindows reads 'RESERVED. This artifact does not mint how long a reader is supported. Product/versioning sets numbers later,' and its authorityClaim records 'the explicit deferral of the evidence/custody/replay-formats matrix with DR-113 (DR202-RR-F3, ADVISORY, STANDS-AS-ROUTED).' Both leftovers are design work, not execution or measurement. D-056 separately lists 'Eligible in kind, not performed: DR-102, DR-115, DR-119, DR-123' and DR-111 is not among them, so nothing in this recording promotes it.

attackListDisposition.result: REFUTED - both verdicts verified at the file level
attackListDisposition.detail: I opened both verdict files and enumerated their finding arrays rather than trusting the draft's summary. Claude 2: verdict ACCEPT, blockers n=0, shouldFix n=0, advisories n=2. Codex: verdict ACCEPT, blockers n=0, shouldFix n=0, advisories n=1. The draft's table states exactly this - 'ACCEPT, 0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 2 advisories' and 'ACCEPT, 0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX, 1 advisory' - and its decision-type line's 'independent dual ACCEPT (0 blockers, 0 SHOULD-FIX from both reviewers)' is correct. Both verdict words are plain ACCEPT, not ACCEPT-WITH-ADVISORIES, and the draft does not overstate them in either direction.

attackListDisposition.result: REFUTED - the disclaimer is correct and uses D-096's own vocabulary
attackListDisposition.detail: Decision 5: 'Does not mint a D-096 (A) grant. Does not dispose DR-117.' I read D-096: it blocks owner-recording 'until both (A) an applicable owner grant covering every named role for the candidate being recorded and (B) separately D-000-reviewed condition-2 owner-recording mechanics,' and warns that 'A mechanics entry alone never grants.' So '(A) grant' is a real construct with that exact meaning, and D-103 disclaims minting one rather than inventing or assuming one. Nothing in the draft grants ownership, names owners, or touches DR-117.

advisories.title: The precedent list groups D-013 and D-015 with D-035 and D-042, but the first two carried a file-08 row edit that this decision declines
advisories.detail: The decision-type line reads 'Same form as D-013 / D-015 / D-035 / D-042.' D-013's decision says 'the register row carries the acceptance. The row edit is this decision's only effect,' and D-015 records the same wording class with its companion row. D-035, D-042 and D-103 carry the recording in the decisions file and do not edit file 08 - D-042 says so explicitly, as does D-103 at decision 4. So on the row-edit axis the four precedents split two and two. I record this as advisory rather than a finding for two reasons: the operative clauses of D-103 state precisely what it does and does not do, so no reader is misled by the body; and D-096 - adopted at 0 MUST-FIX / 0 SHOULD-FIX from both reviewers - already cites 'Same class as D-013 / D-035 / D-042 / D-066' while itself declining the file-08 edit, so loose precedent-class citation is established practice here rather than a defect this draft introduces. A successor could name the split ('recording form as D-035/D-042; row edit deferred to MF-6') to make the citation exact.
advisories.notBlocking: The precedent list is supporting rationale, not an operative clause; every operative clause verified accurate.

advisories.title: The Measured inputs table's first column is headed 'Path' but contains labels and bare filenames, not paths
advisories.detail: The column holds 'compatibility-matrices-contract.v5.json', 'Claude 2 verdict', 'Codex verdict', 'COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md' and 'file 08'. Only the digests are unambiguous, and I resolved all five that way without difficulty. But this corpus's own citation discipline is (path, digest, named property), the sibling artifacts cite full repository-relative paths, and D-042 named its verdict files by full filename. Two of the five entries ('Claude 2 verdict', 'Codex verdict') are role labels that a reader cannot resolve without searching by digest. Supplying the repository-relative paths alongside the digests would make the table self-resolving and cost nothing.
advisories.notBlocking: All five digests resolve to exactly one live file each and all five match, so nothing is ambiguous in practice.

I read its status fields, registerRow, registerRowQuoted, numericWindows, lockJoin and whatThisDoesNotDo only to test D-103's claims about it. The two ACCEPT verdicts stand on their own authority; this review does not re-open them.
I did not verify the internal reasoning of the two v5 verdicts, only their verdict words and finding counts, which is what D-103 asserts.

I did not evaluate whether DR-111's design contract is technically correct, whether the proposed lock-join widening is right, or whether the surfaces list is complete - none of that is what D-103 decides.
I did not read the Codex D-103 review, per the dispatch.
I did not assess DR-111's or any other row's register status beyond confirming DR-111 reads OPEN and condition 2 reads 4 of 30, and I did not edit file 08 or COORDINATOR-DECISIONS.md.
I did not verify D-013's or D-015's file-08 row edits against the register's history; I read their decision text, which states the edits, and treated that as the record.
CONSENT here is to the turn-1 draft as written. It is not an adoption, not a SATISFIED recording, and not an endorsement of any successor that folds the three outstanding advisories.
